examples.en: There is a public restroom in the park, which is convenient.

examples.ko: 공중화장실은 모두가 같이 쓰는 곳이라 깨끗하게 이용해야 해요.
examples.en: A public restroom is shared by everyone, so you should keep it clean.
I walked for a long time looking for a public restroom on the street.
Where is a public restroom near here?
Sometimes there is no toilet paper in a public restroom.
I ran in a hurry to the public restroom at the subway station.

explain: 공원, 지하철역, 길가처럼 누구나 쓰는 화장실이에요. 말할 때는 그냥 '화장실 어디예요?'라고 해도 돼요. '공중화장실'은 안내판이나 뉴스처럼 구분해서 말할 때 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a restroom anyone can use, like those in parks, subway stations and streets. In speech you can simply ask '화장실 어디예요?'. '공중화장실' shows up more on signs and in news, where it needs to be distinguished.

examples.en: I wait for my friend in front of the school gate.
The school gate opens at eight in the morning.
When class ends, students pour out through the gate.
There's a stationery shop next to the gate, which is convenient.
It was raining, so I ran to the school gate.

examples.ko: 늦게 와서 교문이 이미 닫혀 있었어요.
examples.en: I came late and the gate was already closed.

explain: 학교의 정문은 '교문'이라고 많이 불러요. 만날 장소를 말할 때 '교문 앞에서 만나요'라고 자주 해요. 학교 뒤쪽에 있는 문은 '후문'이라고 해요.
explain_en: People often call a school's main gate the 교문. It's a common meeting spot: '교문 앞에서 만나요'. The back gate is the 후문.

examples.en: Taking photos is prohibited here.
The school banned phone use.
My parents don't allow me to go out late at night.

examples.ko: 도서관에서는 큰 소리로 말하는 것을 금지하고 있어요.
examples.en: Talking loudly is prohibited in the library.

examples.ko: 법으로 금지하는 일은 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not do things the law prohibits.

examples.ko: 다음 달부터 이 길에 차를 세우는 것을 금지할 거예요.
examples.en: From next month, parking on this street will be banned.

explain: 법, 규칙, 학교처럼 힘 있는 쪽이 주어일 때 써요. 개인이 가까운 사람에게는 '못 하게 하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 안내문에서는 '주차 금지', '촬영 금지'처럼 명사로 훨씬 많이 봐요. 반대말은 '허락하다', '허용하다'예요.
explain_en: The subject is usually an authority: a law, a rule, or a school. Between individuals, '못 하게 하다' (not let someone do) is more natural. On signs you mostly see the noun, as in '주차 금지' (no parking). The opposites are '허락하다' and '허용하다'.

en: women's section of a public bath house

examples.en: On Sunday I went to the women's bath with my mom.
Excuse me, where is the entrance to the women's bath?
The women's bath is on the right and the men's is on the left.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때 아빠는 남탕, 저는 여탕에 갔어요.
examples.en: When I was little, Dad went to the men's bath and I went to the women's.

examples.ko: 이 목욕탕 여탕에는 작은 사우나도 있어요.
examples.en: The women's side of this bathhouse also has a small sauna.
The women's bath was quiet today, so I washed comfortably.

explain: '남탕'과 짝이 되는 말로, 대중목욕탕 입구에서 많이 보여요. 말로 풀어서 '여자 목욕탕'이라고 하기도 해요. '여탕에 가다'처럼 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 목욕탕 이야기를 할 때만 나와요.
explain_en: It pairs with '남탕' (men's bath) and is commonly seen at the entrance of public bathhouses. It can also be spelled out as '여자 목욕탕'. You say '여탕에 가다', and it mostly comes up when talking about bathhouses.

examples.en: The teacher scolded the students who were playing around.
Don't mess around during class.
My younger sibling keeps pranking me, so I got angry.
The kids play around happily in the park.
I thought my friend was joking, but it was real.
The cat is playing with a ball of yarn.

explain: '장난을 치다'를 줄인 말이고 '누구한테 장난치다'처럼 상대에게 짓궂게 구는 일에도, 물건을 가지고 노는 일에도 써요. '장난치지 마!'는 장난을 그만두라는 말이지만, 진지한 상황에서는 '장난하세요?'처럼 화난 말투가 될 수도 있어요. 놀이를 나타낼 때는 '놀다'가 더 넓은 말이에요.
explain_en: It's a short form of '장난을 치다' and is used both for teasing someone ('누구한테 장난치다') and for playing with objects. '장난치지 마!' tells someone to stop messing around, and in serious situations similar phrases can sound angry. For play in general, '놀다' is the broader word.

examples.en: I bought a canned coffee at the convenience store.
I throw finished cans into the recycling bin.
I made a simple stew with a can of tuna.
The can is so stiff that it is hard to open.

examples.ko: 캔 음료는 병보다 가벼워서 들고 다니기 편해요.
examples.en: Canned drinks are lighter than bottles, so they're easy to carry.

examples.ko: 캠핑 갈 때 캔 음식을 가져가면 편해요.
examples.en: Taking canned food is convenient when you go camping.

explain: 음료나 통조림처럼 금속 통에 든 것은 '캔'이라고 해요. 음식 캔은 '통조림'이라고도 하지만 '참치 캔'처럼 '캔'이 더 자주 나와요. 분리수거에서는 '캔', '병', '페트'로 나눠서 버려요.
explain_en: Things sold in a metal container, like drinks or preserved food, are called 'can'. Food cans are also '통조림', but '참치 캔' (tuna can) with 'can' is heard more. For recycling, Korea sorts into '캔', '병' and '페트'.

examples.ko: 생일 선물로 받은 시계를 팔목에 찼어요.
examples.en: I put on the watch I got as a birthday present on my wrist.
I hurt my wrist when I fell on the stairs.
My wrist hurts, so it is hard to use a mouse.
My friend grabbed my wrist tightly.
The sleeves are short, so my whole wrist shows.
I rolled my sleeves up to the wrist.

explain: '손목'도 같은 부분을 가리켜서 시계나 팔찌 이야기에서 둘 다 들을 수 있어요. 시계는 '차다'를 써서 '팔목에 차다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '손목' points to the same part, so you may hear both when people talk about watches or bracelets. A watch goes with '차다', as in '팔목에 차다'.

examples.en: Please don't act like a child in meetings.
You must behave quietly in a library.

examples.ko: 화가 날 때는 생각하고 나서 행동하세요.
examples.en: When you're angry, think first, then act.
That person always behaves kindly.
I behaved strangely yesterday.
Talking is easy, but acting is hard.

explain: '조용히', '친절하게', '이상하게'처럼 어떻게 하는지 말이 꼭 같이 나와요. '말'과 비교해서 몸으로 실제로 하는 것을 가리킬 때도 잘 쓰고요. 가볍게 말할 때는 '굴다'도 쓰는데 '왜 그렇게 굴어요?'처럼 불만이 담겨요. 명사는 '행동을 하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It almost always comes with a manner word like '조용히' (quietly), '친절하게' (kindly), or '이상하게' (strangely). It also contrasts doing with saying, as in '말은 쉽지만 행동하기는 어려워요'. A casual alternative is '굴다', which carries annoyance: '왜 그렇게 굴어요?' The noun can be used as '행동을 하다' too.
